alerts.title: EFV neuropsychiatric toxicity: insomnia and vivid dreams
alerts.message: Guidelines list insomnia as a recognized toxicity of ARVs and provide EFV-specific management: if on EFV 600mg, lower the dose to 400mg; if on EFV 400mg, reassure, and if symptoms persist, substitute EFV with DTG. EFV 400mg has fewer adverse events than 600mg. Patient has been on EFV since February 2024 and presents with poor sleep and vivid dreams for several weeks. EFV is a well-known cause of neuropsychiatric side effects including insomnia and vivid dreams, supporting drug attribution. No alternative causes such as anxiety, depression, or substance use are documented, though these should be excluded. The clinician's plan does not address dose adjustment or substitution.

evidence.recommended_action: If on EFV 600mg, reduce to 400mg. If already on 400mg, reassure; if symptoms persist, substitute EFV with DTG. Exclude other causes of insomnia.

alerts.title: Viral load monitoring overdue
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend routine viral load monitoring for adults at 6 and 12 months after ART initiation, then every 12 months thereafter. Patient started ART in February 2024; the last viral load was on 2025-08-10 (approximately 12 months after initiation). The next routine viral load is now overdue as of the 2026-01-22 visit, approximately 165 days since the last test. The clinician's plan does not include a viral load order.

evidence.recommended_action: Order a routine viral load test at this visit, as the annual monitoring interval has elapsed since the last test in August 2025.

alerts.title: Low-level viremia on last viral load
alerts.message: Guidelines note that viral load above 200 copies/mL is associated with risk of sexual transmission and subsequent virologic non-suppression, and incorporate WHO guidance to monitor low-level viremia. Patient's last viral load was 60 copies/mL, which is below the suppression cutoff of 200 copies/mL but represents detectable low-level viremia. This warrants enhanced monitoring to confirm re-suppression and rule out emerging resistance. No repeat viral load was ordered in the clinician's plan.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat viral load to confirm re-suppression, given detectable low-level viremia at 60 copies/mL on the last test.
